meta.title: Directive 2010/64/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 20 October 2010 on the right to interpretation and translation in criminal proceedings

items.heading: Article 1

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment:
Too general to transpose.


The official position of the Polish government is that the Directive 2010/64 has been fully transposed. However, in fact the transposition can hardly be assessed as done - compare comments below regarding detailed provisions of the Directive. The comments are expression of experts own assessment backed by references to Polish legal doctrine and case-law.

items.text: 1. This Directive lays down rules concerning the right to interpretation and translation in criminal proceedings and proceedings for the execution of a European arrest warrant.

2. The right referred to in paragraph 1 shall apply to persons from the time that they are made aware by the competent authorities of a Member State, by official notification or otherwise, that they are suspected or accused of having committed a criminal offence until the conclusion of the proceedings, which is understood to mean the final determination of the question whether they have committed the offence, including, where applicable, sentencing and the resolution of any appeal.

nationalActs.title: Ustawa z dnia 6 czerwca 1997 r. - Kodeks postępowania karnego
nationalActs.titleEn: Law of 6 June 1997 - Code of Criminal Procedure

provisions.textEn:
§ 1. A suspect is a person, with regard to whom a decision presenting charges was issued, or who, without the issuance of such a decision, was informed about the charges in connection with his interrogation in the capacity of a suspect.


§ 2. An accused is a person, against whom an indictment was submitted to a court, and also a person, with regard to whom a public prosecutor has filed a request referred to in Article 335 § 1 or a request for a conditional discontinuation of proceedings.


§ 3. If the term “accused” is used in this Code with a general meaning, relevant provisions apply also to the suspect.

§ 1. If information existing at the moment of initiating the investigation or collected during the investigation sufficiently justifies the suspicion that the offence was committed by a specific individual, a written decision to bring charges is drawn up. It is immediately announced to the suspect and the suspect is interrogated, unless the announcement of the decision and the interrogation are not possible because the suspect is hiding or abroad.


§ 2. The written decision to bring charges shall indicate the suspect, an exact description of the offence and its legal qualification.


§ 3. The suspect may - until he is notified of the date of final disclosure of the case file at the end of investigation - demand that the grounds of the charges are explained to him verbally, as well as that a written statement of reasons is drawn up. The suspect has to be advised of these rights. The statement of reasons is served upon the suspect and the appointed defence counsel within 14 days.


§ 4. The statement of reasons should clarify in particular on what facts and evidence the charges are based.
The provisions concerning investigation apply accordingly to inquiry, unless the provisions of this Chapter state otherwise.

provisions.comment: This provision only applies in inquiry and it modifies the rules of formal charging that are applied in the investigation.
provisions.textEn:
§ 1. It is not required to issue a written decision to bring charges or to issue a decision to close an inquiry, unless the suspect is detained on remand.


§ 2. The interrogation of a person suspected of an offence starts with information on the charges which are specified in the transcript of the interrogation. This person is considered as a suspect from the beginning of the interrogation.

items.comment:
According to Polish law only a person formally charged with a crime during criminal investigation is granted a status of podejrzany and provided with certain rights including a right to access to a lawyer, right to remain silent, right to legal aid etc. This charging decision however, can be considered only as a preliminary charging decision and does not involve the court in any way. In particular, it cannot be considered as equal to filing a case with a court with an aim to accuse a person with a crime. This is done later at the end of criminal investigation in the form of indictment which makes podejrzany to become oskarżony - a party to court proceedings with all rights available to him or her at this stage of criminal process. 
Note that both colloquially and in official wording of Polish version of Directive the word podejrzany is translated from Polish to English as suspect. This causes misunderstanding and misinterpretation of whether Directives are properly and fully implemented or not.
In the light of the above, one can assume, as it is done so by the Polish government, that the Polish criminal procedure remains in compliance with the EU Directive since podejrzany in Polish legal system is guaranteed all rights provided in Directives for the suspect. But such an interpretation is inconsistent with the meaning of the concept of a suspect as used in Directives. The Polish definition of podejrzany does not encompass the individual against whom the criminal investigation is aimed being arrested or searched but not yet formally charged with a crime. The Polish law provides for such an individual a separate name i.e. osoba podejrzana (translated directly as suspected person) and does not provide for her the same protection that the podejrzany is normally provided with. Some limited protection is only provided in case osoba podejrzana is arrested. E.g. she may be assisted by a lawyer free of charge, but the latter has status of legal counsel not a defence counsel. The main difference is the scope of legal privilege available for the individual. The defence counsel cannot be questioned as witness in relation to his or her contact with the client, whereas the legal counsel can be questioned as witness in relation to his or her contact with the client (excluding cases where he or she advises arrested person). Moreover, the legal counsel does not have unlimited right to participate in questioning or other actions undertaken by the investigating authorities. 
As a result, it should be acknowledged that the Polish law does not remain in full compliance with the EU Directives since the suspect who is osoba podejrzana (until formal preliminary charges are laid out against her during investigation) is not entitled to the same protection that is given to podejrzany. In order to assume that the EU Directives are properly and fully implemented in Poland the guarantees provided for the suspect should be extended also to those individuals who acquired status of osoba podejrzana and are not yet preliminarily charged with a crime.

items.text: 3. Where the law of a Member State provides for the imposition of a sanction regarding minor offences by an authority other than a court having jurisdiction in criminal matters, and the imposition of such a sanction may be appealed to such a court, this Directive shall apply only to the proceedings before that court following such an appeal.

4. This Directive does not affect national law concerning the presence of legal counsel during any stage of the criminal proceedings, nor does it affect national law concerning the right of access of a suspected or accused person to documents in criminal proceedings.

items.heading: Article 2

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that suspected or accused persons who do not speak or understand the language of the criminal proceedings concerned are provided, without delay, with interpretation during criminal proceedings before investigative and judicial authorities, including during police questioning, all court hearings and any necessary interim hearings.

nationalActs.title: Ustawa z dnia 6 czerwca 1997 r. - Kodeks postępowania karnego
nationalActs.titleEn: Law of 6 June 1997 - Code of Criminal Procedure

provisions.textEn: § 1. An accused, who does not have a sufficient command of Polish, is entitled to the gratuitous help of an interpreter (translator).
The interpreter (translator) should be summoned to assist in all activities with the participation of the accused referred to in § 1.

§ 1. An interpreter (translator) is summoned if there is a need for the examination of:

1) a person, who is deaf or mute and written communication is not sufficient,

2) a person who has no command of Polish.

§ 2. An interpreter (translator) should also be summoned if there is a need to translate a document drawn up in a foreign language to Polish or vice versa or to familiarise a party to the proceedings with the content of the evidence.
If the word “accused” is used in this Code as a general term, relevant provisions apply to suspect as well.

§ 2 The arrestee is immediately informed of the reasons for the arrest and of his rights, including the right to use the assistance of an advocate or legal counsel and a gratuitous help of an interpreter, if the arrestee does not have a sufficient command of Polish, to make statements and to refuse making statements, to obtain copy of an arrest report, to have access to medical first aid, as well as of his rights indicated in Article 245, Article 246 § 1 and Article 612 § 2 and of the contents of Article 248 § 1 and 2. The arrestee’s explanations should also be heard.

§ 5. The Minister of Justice shall define by way of a regulation the form of the instruction referred to in § 2, containing in particular the information on the rights vested in the accused: to use a free-of-charge assistance of an interpreter, to make a statement and to refuse making a statement concerning the arrest, to obtain access to the medical first aid, as well as of the rights specified in § 2, Article 245, Article 246 § 1 and Article 612 § 2 and information on the contents of Article 248 § 1 and 2, bearing in mind also the necessity of making the instruction comprehensible to the persons not using the assistance of an attorney.

items.comment: The provision is transposed with regard to accused and suspect as defined in the Polish law. However, compare remarks to art. 1 (2) of this Directive as to the notion of suspect in Polish law, which is not fully consistent with the European one. Therefore, one should assess separately the position of a suspected person, who is perceived as a supect within the meaning of the Directive but is not suspect regarding to Polish law if formal charges has not yet been presented. Such person is to be assisted by an interpreter during police questioning or when he or she is arrested. Not all court hearings or interim hearings with suspected person involved are however covered by Polish regulation since specific provisions only concern questioning and arrestees. If a suspected person has not been arrested but has for example been searched and filed an interlocutory appeal to review such search, there is no provision guaranteeing him or her the right to interpreter on the hearing regarding the appeal which means that the provision has not been transposed.

items.text: 2. Member States shall ensure that, where necessary for the purpose of safeguarding the fairness of the proceedings, interpretation is available for communication between suspected or accused persons and their legal counsel in direct connection with any questioning or hearing during the proceedings or with the lodging of an appeal or other procedural applications.

nationalActs.title: Ustawa z dnia 6 czerwca 1997 r. - Kodeks postępowania karnego
nationalActs.titleEn: Law of 6 June 1997 - Code of Criminal Procedure

provisions.comment: Amendment introduced by Act amending CCP of 27 Sept 2013 (entered into force Nov 9th 2013)
provisions.textEn: Upon request of the accused or his defence counsel, the interpreter (translator) should also be summoned in order to assist in communication between the accused and defence counsel in connection with any step (action) in proceedings, in which the accused is entitled to participate.
If the word “accused” is used in this Code as a general term, relevant provisions apply to suspect as well.

§ 1. An interpreter (translator) is summoned if there is a need for the examination of:

1) a person, who is deaf or mute and written communication is not sufficient,

2) a person who has no command of Polish.

§ 2. An interpreter (translator) should also be summoned if there is a need to translate a document drawn up in a foreign language to Polish or vice versa or to familiarise a party to the proceedings with the content of the evidence

items.comment:
On a statutory basis art. 2 (2) of the Directive seems transposed. However, there are no precise provisions as to what particular steps should be taken by the accused or his or her counsel in order to execute this right and no relevant case law. Also the notion of “steps (actions) in which the accused is entitled to participate” may cause doubts as to whether it covers situations of lodging an appeal or other procedural applications, which are expressly mentioned in the Directive. Nevertheless, in the doctrine it is understood that the notion of communication in connection with such actions should be interpreted as covering also contacts in order to decide whether any actions should be taken, including appeal measures (see S. Steinborn, in: S. Steinborn (red.), Kodeks postępowania karnego. Komentarz do wybranych przepisów, LEX 2016/el.). Clarifying in the Code itsfelf would nevertheless be desirable. 

In addition, due to problems with the inconsistency between the Polish and European notion of suspect, the right is only guaranteed for supects that have formally been charged. Compare remarks to art. 1 (2) of this Directive.

items.text: 3. The right to interpretation under paragraphs 1 and 2 includes appropriate assistance for persons with hearing or speech impediments.

nationalActs.title: Ustawa z dnia 6 czerwca 1997 r. - Kodeks postępowania karnego
nationalActs.titleEn: Law of 6 June 1997 - Code of Criminal Procedure

provisions.textEn: § 1. An accused, who does not have a sufficient command of Polish, is entitled to the gratuitous help of an interpreter (translator).
The interpreter (translator) should be summoned to assist in all activities with the participation of the accused referred to in § 1.
If the word “accused” is used in this Code as a general term, relevant provisions apply to suspect as well.

items.comment: There are serious doubts expressed in the legal doctrine as to whether the right is transposed to Polish Code. Art. 72 CCP, which regulates the right of the suspect and accused to interpretation, expressly addresses only lack of knowledge of Polish language and not the disability to hear or speak. It is pointed out that the literal wording of this provision cannot be approved and that article 204 § 1 CCP does not fully compensate this fault as it only guarantees the right to interpretation in the course of examination of such person. It is argued that art. 72 CCP should be understood as covering also the right to interpretation of persons with hearing or speech impediments (S. Steinborn, in: S. Steinborn (red.), Kodeks postępowania karnego. Komentarz do wybranych przepisów, LEX 2016/el.). Nevertheless, judging only by the wording of the CCP, the right has not been fully transposed.

items.text: 4. Member States shall ensure that a procedure or mechanism is in place to ascertain whether suspected or accused persons speak and understand the language of the criminal proceedings and whether they need the assistance of an interpreter.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment: There is no procedure or mechanism of ascertaining whether the accused or suspect speak and understand Polish. It is established by the Police, prosecutor or the court depending on the stage of proceedings with the use of any available data. It is thus doubtful whether the provision has been transposed at all.

items.text: 5. Member States shall ensure that, in accordance with procedures in national law, suspected or accused persons have the right to challenge a decision finding that there is no need for interpretation and, when interpretation has been provided, the possibility to complain that the quality of the interpretation is not sufficient to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings.

nationalActs.title: Ustawa z dnia 6 czerwca 1997 r. - Kodeks postępowania karnego
nationalActs.titleEn: Law of 6 June 1997 - Code of Criminal Procedure

provisions.textEn:
§ 2. Parties and persons who are not parties to the proceedings may appeal against procedures other than decisions and orders, if such procedures violate their rights.

§ 3. Interlocutory appeals against decisions, orders and other procedures conducted by the public prosecutor in preparatory proceedings are considered by a directly superior public prosecutor.

The judgment is reversed or changed if it is found that:

1) the provisions of substantive law regarding legal qualification of the act were violated,

1a) the provisions of substantive law other than mentioned in point 1) were violated, unless the judgment reflects the law despite wrong legal basis

2) the provisions of procedural law were violated, if this might have affected the contents of the judgment,

3) the findings on which the judgment is based were established incorrectly, if this might have affected the contents of the judgment,

4) a penalty, a penal measure or the obligation to compensate for a harm imposed is egregiously disproportionate or a preventive, forfeiture or other measure was incorrectly imposed or the court incorrectly failed to impose it.
The parties and other directly interested persons may request the performance of actions, even when the authorities are able or obliged to undertake ex officio.

The provisions concerning expert witnesses apply accordingly to interpreters

(translators).

If the expert witness’s statement is incomplete, unclear or contradictory or if there are contradictions between different statements issued in the same case, the court may summon the same experts again or appoint new ones.

items.comment:
There is no separate mechanism or remedy for the purpose of challenging the decision on refusal of the right to interpretation. In fact such refusal – if it happens – is not a formal decision but rather a matter of fact. Such refusal may be contested in an appeal from the judgment or an interlocutory appeal on any of the incidental decisions as a fault in procedure. At the stage of preparatory proceedings it may also be challenged as an action other than decision or order (i.e. factual action) violating suspect’s rights (art. 302 § 2 CCP). The provision of the directive is nevertheless not fully transposed since the possibility mentioned above is only a creative interpretation of existing mechanisms which were not designed for the purpose of challenging refusal of interpretation.


There is no specific mechanism of complaining on the quality of interpretation. Nevertheless the parties to the proceedings may file for any necessary actions of the authorities any time in the course of proceedings. However, a suspected person, i.e. a person who has not yet been formally presented with the charges but there are procedural investigative or other actions conducted against him or her, is not a party to proceedings (compare the remarks to art. 1 (2) of this Directive). What also needs to be underlined is that the role of the interpretator is regulated with the mutatis mutandis use of the provision concerning expert witnesses whose work may be questioned on the grounds of incompleteness, ambiguity or incongruence. Bearing that in mind, the provision is partially transposed.

items.text: 6. Where appropriate, communication technology such as videoconferencing, telephone or the Internet may be used, unless the physical presence of the interpreter is required in order to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment:
There are three situations when the accused may be entitled and at the same time may be forced to take part in a procedural activity without his personal presence, i.e. via videoconference:

  1. a court hearing on pre-trial detention in preparatory proceedings,
  2. main trial in special accelarated proceedings,
  3. main trial in any proceedings if the accused is deprived of liberty.

In first of these situations, the law is imprecise but does seem to provide that the general rule is that the interpreter is present at court, but he or she may be present wherever the accused is present. In the second one, the interpreter is present at the location of the accused. In the latter case, the general rule is that the interpreter is present at the location of the accused, but the chairman may decide otherwise.


Polish legislator did not introduce any provision allowing the interpreter to act via communication technology, which leads to the conclusion that physical presence of the interpreter always has to be guaranteed as there are no provisions stating otherwise.

items.text: 7. In proceedings for the execution of a European arrest warrant, the executing Member State shall ensure that its competent authorities provide persons subject to such proceedings who do not speak or understand the language of the proceedings with interpretation in accordance with this Article.

nationalActs.title: Ustawa z dnia 6 czerwca 1997 r. - Kodeks postępowania karnego
nationalActs.titleEn: Law of 6 June 1997 - Code of Criminal Procedure

provisions.comment: Amendment introduced by Act amending CCP of 27 Sept 2013 (entered into force June 2nd 2014)
provisions.textEn: The Minister of Justice shall define by way of a regulation the form of the instruction for a person requested by a European warrant, informing him of his rights in case of arrest: to obtain information on the contents of the warrant, to consent to the surrender, to make statements concerning the surrender, to be assisted by a defence counsel, to provide explanations and to refuse providing explanations, to review the files in the part concerning the reasons for the arrest, to obtain access to the medical first aid, as well as of the rights specified in in § 3, in Article 72 § 1, Article 78 § 1, Article 261 § 1, 2 and 2a, Article 612 and of the contents of Article 607k § 3 and 3a, bearing in mind also the necessity of making the instruction comprehensible to the persons not assisted by an attorney.
An accused, who does not have a sufficient command of Polish, is entitled to the gratuitous help of an interpreter (translator).
The interpreter (translator) should be summoned to assist in all activities with the participation of the accused referred to in § 1.

§ 1. An interpreter (translator) is summoned if there is a need for the examination of:

1) a person, who is deaf or mute and written communication is not sufficient,

2) a person who has no command of Polish.

§ 2. An interpreter (translator) should also be summoned if there is a need to translate a document drawn up in a foreign language to Polish or vice versa or to familiarise a party to the proceedings with the content of the evidence.

items.comment: Firstly, it is stated in the legal doctrine, the provisions concerning the suspect and accused persons should be applied accordingly to requested person who enjoys the same general right to interpretations. Secondly, the Constitutional Tribunal in its judgment of October 5th 2010, SK 26/08, stated that the requested person enjoys the rights of the accused. Lastly, a specific provision introduced an obligation to inform the requested person who is arrested of the right to interpretation, which makes it clearer that they enjoy such right.

items.text: 8. Interpretation provided under this Article shall be of a quality sufficient to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings, in particular by ensuring that suspected or accused persons have knowledge of the case against them and are able to exercise their right of defence.

nationalActs.title: Ustawa z dnia 25 listopada 2004 r. o zawodzie tłumacza przysięgłego
nationalActs.titleEn: Law of November 25th 2004 on the profession of sworn interpreter (translator)

nationalActs.title: Ustawa z dnia 6 czerwca 1997 r. - Kodeks postępowania karnego
nationalActs.titleEn: Law of 6 June 1997 - Code of Criminal Procedure

provisions.textEn: The provisions concerning expert witnesses apply accordingly to interpreters.
The duties of an expert witness are performed not only by an expert enlisted by the court in the registry, but also by any person known to have adequate knowledge in a given area.

items.comment: The legal position of the interpreter in criminal proceedings is to be established by applying provisions regarding expert witnesses accordingly. This means that an interpreter may be either a sworn interpreter (who acquired this position in accordance with the Act of November 25th 2004 on the profession of sworn interpreter/translator) or an ad hoc interpreter, appointed by the investigating authority or the court for the purpose of particular criminal proceedings due to one’s expert knowledge of the language. In the latter case, assessing whether this knowledge is enough to provide sufficient quality belongs to the investigating authority or the court. Thus, the transposition is full only with respect to sworn interpreters.

items.heading: Article 3
items.subHeading: Right to translation of essential documents

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that suspected or accused persons who do not understand the language of the criminal proceedings concerned are, within a reasonable period of time, provided with a written translation of all documents which are essential to ensure that they are able to exercise their right of defence and to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings.

nationalActs.title: Ustawa z dnia 6 czerwca 1997 r. - Kodeks postępowania karnego
nationalActs.titleEn: Law of 6 June 1997 - Code of Criminal Procedure

provisions.textEn:
§ 1. An accused, who does not have a sufficient command of Polish, is entitled to the gratuitous help of an interpreter (translator).

(...)

§ 3. The decision presenting, supplementing or changing charges, an indictment, as well as a judgment which may be subject to an appeal or which ends the proceedings must be served upon the accused referred to in § 1 with a translation. With the consent of the accused, it is sufficient to announce the translated judgment ending the proceedings, if it is not subject to appeal.

§ 2 The arrestee is immediately informed of the reasons for the arrest and of his rights, including the right to use the assistance of an advocate or legal counsel and a gratuitous help of an interpreter, if the arrestee does not have a sufficient command of Polish, to make statements and to refuse making statements, to obtain copy of an arrest report, to have access to medical first aid, as well as of his rights indicated in Article 245, Article 246 § 1 and Article 612 § 2 and of the contents of Article 248 § 1 and 2. The arrestee’s explanations should also be heard.

(...)

§ 5. The Minister of Justice shall define by way of a regulation the form of the instruction referred to in § 2, containing in particular the information on the rights vested in the accused: to use a free-of-charge assistance of an interpreter, to make a statement and to refuse making a statement concerning the arrest, to obtain access to the medical first aid, as well as of the rights specified in § 2, Article 245, Article 246 § 1 and Article 612 § 2 and information on the contents of Article 248 § 1 and 2, bearing in mind also the necessity of making the instruction comprehensible to the persons not using the assistance of an attorney.
If the word “accused” is used in this Code as a general term, relevant provisions apply to suspect as well.

items.comment:
In general the right to translation is guaranteed. There are however serious doubts as to the notion of “essential documents”. The Supreme Court has indicated in of its judgments that it is not required to translate the entire case file in writing, but only the materials necessary to ensure that the accused have a fair trial (judgment of April 4th 2012, III KK 133/11, LEX no. 1213392). One can find judgments representing both narrow and wide interpretations of the notion of “essential documents”. There is no consent as to whether this notion covers expert witnesses’ written statements or appeal measures of other parties – although a positive answer is recommended by the doctrine (see M. Matusiak-Frącczak, Prawo do tłumaczenia istotnych dokumentów w sprawach karnych. Glosa do wyroku TS z dnia 12 października 2017 r., C-278/16).

Compare also remarks concerning Art. 3 (2) of the Directive as to the scope of this right. 

Please compare also remarks concerning Art. 1 (2) of this Directive, regarding incompliance of the notion of suspect in Polish law with the notion of suspect used in the Directive. Due to this inconsistency, one should discuss separately assess the position of a suspected person who has not yet been formally presented with charges. Such person’s right to translation is not guaranteed unless he or she is arrested.

items.text: 2. Essential documents shall include any decision depriving a person of his liberty, any charge or indictment, and any judgment.

nationalActs.title: Ustawa z dnia 6 czerwca 1997 r. - Kodeks postępowania karnego
nationalActs.titleEn: Law of 6 June 1997 - Code of Criminal Procedure

provisions.textEn:
§ 1. An accused, who does not have a sufficient command of Polish, is entitled to the gratuitous help of an interpreter (translator).


(...)


§ 3. The decision presenting, supplementing or changing charges, an indictment, as well as a judgment which may be subject to an appeal or which ends the proceedings must be served upon the accused referred to in § 1 with a translation. With the consent of the accused, it is sufficient to announce the translated judgment ending the proceedings, if an appeal against it is not admissible.

An interpreter (translator) should also be called if there is a need to translate a document drawn up in a foreign language to Polish or vice versa or to familiarise a party to the proceedings with the content of the evidence.

items.comment: The transposition is not full. Charge and indictment are always provided with translation, as well as any judgment (as it is either subject to appeal or ends proceedings). Nevertheless the analysis of Polish provisions leads to the conclusion that suspect or accused do not have the right to be served with a written translation of the appeal court’s decision to uphold a pretrial detention order because it is not subject to further appeal and is not expressly covered by art. 72 CCP although it is decision which should be seen as depriving of one’s liberty. However, there is a legal basis in art. 204 § 2 CCP to call the translator whenever there is “a need” to translate a document. Also, whenever a suspected person, suspect or accused is apprehended on the basis of a written decision and not on an ad hoc basis, the decision itself is not subject to appeal (only the act of apprehension is), which means it is not served with translation. That is because Polish provisions do not mention among essential documents decision depriving a person of his or her liberty as such but they mention judgments which may be subject to an appeal instead.

items.text: 3. The competent authorities shall, in any given case, decide whether any other document is essential. Suspected or accused persons or their legal counsel may submit a reasoned request to that effect.

nationalActs.title: Ustawa z dnia 6 czerwca 1997 r. - Kodeks postępowania karnego
nationalActs.titleEn: Law of 6 June 1997 - Code of Criminal Procedure

provisions.textEn: An interpreter (translator) should also be called if there is a need to translate a document drawn up in a foreign language to Polish or vice versa or to familiarise a party to the proceedings with the content of the evidence.
The parties and other directly interested persons may request the performance of actions, even when the authorities are able or obliged to undertake ex officio.

items.comment: The provision has not been explicitly transposed. However, there is a legal basis in art. 204 § 2 CCP to call the translator whenever there is “a need” to translate a document, There are thus no obstacles for the authorities to provide the accused with translated documents other than expressly mentioned in the law (see Art. 3 (2) of the Directive) on their own initiative or if the accused or his or her counsel apply for it.

items.text: 4. There shall be no requirement to translate passages of essential documents which are not relevant for the purposes of enabling suspected or accused persons to have knowledge of the case against them.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment: Not suitable for transposition

items.text: 5. Member States shall ensure that, in accordance with procedures in national law, suspected or accused persons have the right to challenge a decision finding that there is no need for the translation of documents or passages thereof and, when a translation has been provided, the possibility to complain that the quality of the translation is not sufficient to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings.

The judgment is reversed or changed if it is found that:

1) the provisions of substantive law regarding legal qualification of the act were violated,

1a) the provisions of substantive law other than mentioned in point 1) were violated, unless the judgment reflects the law despite wrong legal basis,

2) the provisions of procedural law were violated, if this might have affected the contents of the judgment,

Bearing that in mind, the provision is transposed.

items.text: 6. In proceedings for the execution of a European arrest warrant, the executing Member State shall ensure that its competent authorities provide any person subject to such proceedings who does not understand the language in which the European arrest warrant is drawn up, or into which it has been translated by the issuing Member State, with a written translation of that document.

nationalActs.titleEn: Law of 6 June 1997 - Code of Criminal Procedure

provisions.comment: § 1a introduced by Act amending CCP of 27 Sept 2013 (entered into force 9 Nov 2013)
provisions.textEn:
§ 1. The court adjudicates with respect to the surrender and detention on remand in a hearing, in which the public prosecutor and the defence counsel may participate.

§ 1a. When notifying the prosecuted person of the hearing referred to in § 1, the court serves the European warrant together with the translation obtained from the public prosecutor. If due to particular circumstances it is not possible to prepare the translation before the hearing, the translation is ordered by the court. The court may limit itself to the notification of the prosecuted person of the contents of the European warrant if it does not hinder the realisation of this person’s rights, including those mentioned under § 2.

§ 2. If the requested person expresses such a wish, the court will take from him and record in the transcript the declaration of consent to the surrender or of consent to Article 607e § 1 not being applied. The declaration may not be withdrawn, of which fact the requested person should be advised.

items.text: 7. As an exception to the general rules established in paragraphs 1, 2, 3 and 6, an oral translation or oral summary of essential documents may be provided instead of a written translation on condition that such oral translation or oral summary does not prejudice the fairness of the proceedings.

provisions.textEn:
§ 1. The court adjudicates with respect to the surrender and detention on remand in a hearing, in which the public prosecutor and the defence counsel may participate.

§ 1a. When notifying the prosecuted person of the hearing referred to in § 1, the court serves the European warrant together with the translation obtained from the public prosecutor. If due to particular circumstances it is not possible to prepare the translation before the hearing, the translation is ordered by the court. The court may limit itself to the notification of the prosecuted person of the contents of the European warrant if it does not hinder the realisation of this person’s rights, including those mentioned under § 2.

§ 2. If the requested person expresses such a wish, the court will take from him and record in the transcript the declaration of consent to the surrender or of consent to Article 607e § 1 not being applied. The declaration may not be withdrawn, of which fact the requested person should be advised.

The decision presenting, supplementing or changing charges, an indictment, as well as a judgment which may be subject to an appeal or which ends the proceedings must be served upon the accused referred to in § 1 with a translation. With the consent of the accused, it is sufficient to announce the translated judgment ending the proceedings, if an appeal against it is not admissible.
If the word “accused” is used in this Code as a general term, relevant provisions apply to suspect as well.

items.comment: The exception from the delivery of full motion to the requested person meets the standard of the directive. However, it is doubtful whether in the field of general criminal proceedings the exception from mandatory written translation which is possible with the consent of the accused when there is no appeal from the decision has the equal meaning with the Directive's requirement of guaranteeing the fairness of proceedings.

items.text: 8. Any waiver of the right to translation of documents referred to in this Article shall be subject to the requirements that suspected or accused persons have received prior legal advice or have otherwise obtained full knowledge of the consequences of such a waiver, and that the waiver was unequivocal and given voluntarily.

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment: There is no provision allowing the suspect or accused to waive the right to translation (other than those referred to in section 7 above allowing the right to waive the right to written translation while keeping the right to interpretation at the same time). Delivering a translation required by the law is always the duty of the investigating authority or the court.

items.text: 9. Translation provided under this Article shall be of a quality sufficient to safeguard the fairness of the proceedings, in particular by ensuring that suspected or accused persons have knowledge of the case against them and are able to exercise their right of defence.

provisions.textEn: The provisions concerning expert witnesses apply accordingly to interpreters (translators).
The duties of an expert witness are performed not only by an expert enlisted by the court in the registry, but also by any person known to have adequate knowledge in a given area.

items.comment: The legal position of the translator in criminal proceedings is to be established by applying provisions regarding expert witnesses accordingly. This means that an interpreter may be either a sworn translator (who acquired this position in accordance with the Act of November 25th 2004 on the profession of sworn interpreter/translator) or an ad hoc translator, appointed by the investigating authority or the court for the purpose of particular criminal proceedings due to one’s expert knowledge of the language. In the latter case, assessing whether this knowledge is enough to provide sufficient quality belongs to the investigating authority or the court. Thus, the transposition is full only with respect to sworn translators.

items.text: Member States shall meet the costs of interpretation and translation resulting from the application of Articles 2 and 3, irrespective of the outcome of the proceedings.

provisions.textEn: An accused, who does not have a sufficient command of Polish, is entitled to the gratuitous help of an interpreter.
If the word “accused” is used in this Code as a general term, relevant provisions apply to suspect as well.

§ 1. Costs of court proceedings include:

1) court costs,

2) justified expenses of parties, including costs of retaining one defence counsel or attorney.

§ 2. Court costs include:

1) fees,

2) expenses incurred by the State Treasury from the initiation of proceedings.

§ 1. The expenses of the State Treasury include in particular expenses incurred in connection with:

(…)

7) fees of witnesses and interpreters (translators),

(…) .
The court awards court costs to the benefit of the State Treasury and expenses to the benefit of the subsidiary prosecutor against a person convicted in a case prosecuted by public accusation.

items.comment: Although there is no express regulation excluding the costs of interpretation and translation from the costs of proceedings which are to be borne by the accused in case of conviction, the relevant case law of the Supreme Court is clear that the provision of art. 72 § 1 CCP (right to free assistance of interpreter) prevails over the general rules on costs of proceedings (see Supreme Court decision of 13th Sept 2016, V KK 36/16, OSNKW 2016/11/77).

items.heading: Article 5
items.subHeading: Quality of the interpretation and translation

items.text: 1. Member States shall take concrete measures to ensure that the interpretation and translation provided meets the quality required under Article 2(8) and Article 3(9).

nationalActs.title: Ustawa z dnia 25 listopada 2004 r. o zawodzie tłumacza przysięgłego
nationalActs.titleEn: Law of November 25th 2004 on the profession of sworn interpreter (translator)

provisions.textEn:
In order to become a sworn interpreter (translator) a physical person has to fulfill conditions hereinbelow stated:

1) be a Polish citizen or a citizen of another state of the EU, state-party to EFTA or EEA, Switzerland or another state if it is stated in the EU law that he or she has the right to be employed or establish an enterprise within the EU or another state on the basis of reciprocity, 

2) know Polish language;

3) have full legal capacity    

4) have not been convicted of a willful crime, tax crime or an unwillful crime against the safety of economic market

5) have a University degree  

6) passed an exam in translation from Polish to foreign language and from foreign language to Polish.

1. The exam for sworn interpreters (translators) consists of 2 parts:

1) written translation from Polish to foreign language and from foreign language to Polish,

2) oral interpretation from Polish to foreign language and from foreign language to Polish.

2. The exam is considered passed only in case of acquiring positive grades from both parts mentioned in section 1.

Sworn interpreter (translator) is obliged to:

1) execute their duties with particular care and impartiality, in accordance with the law,

2) keep in secret facts and circumstances he got to know while interpreting (translating);

3) improve their professional qualifications.

provisions.textEn: The provisions concerning experts apply accordingly to interpreters (transplators).

§ 1. Persons mentioned in Article 178, 182 and 185, as well as persons, who are disqualified for the reasons listed in Article 40 § 1 points 1-3 and 5 or summoned to act as a witness in a given case or who witnessed the offence, may not be called as experts.

§ 2. If the reasons for the disqualification of an expert mentioned in § 1 come to light, the opinion issued by him does not constitute evidence and - in place of the disqualified expert - a new expert is appointed.

§ 3. If information is revealed that undermines confidence in the expert’s knowledge or impartiality, or other important information, a new expert is appointed.

It is not permitted to examine as a witness:

1) a defence counsel or an advocate or legal advisor acting pursuant to Article 245 § 1 (legal help for apprehended persons) with regard to facts learned while giving legal advice or conducting a case,

2) a clergyman with regard to facts learned during confession.

§ 1. The next of kin to the accused may refuse to testify.

§ 2. The right to refuse to testify continues despite the fact that the marriage or adoption was terminated.

§ 3. The right to refuse to testify is also vested in a witness who is accused of being an accomplice in the crime in question in a separate trial in progress.
A person in a particularly close personal relationship with the accused may be released from the obligation to testify or to answer questions, if such a person applies for such a release.

§ 1. A judge is disqualified by virtue of law from participation in a case where:

1)  the case concerns him personally,

2)  he is a spouse to the party, to the aggrieved party or their defence counsel, attorney, legal representative or cohabits with one of these persons,

3)  he is a relative by blood or by marriage in a direct line, and in a collateral way up to the children of siblings of the persons specified in point 2 or is related to any of those persons by adoption, guardianship or custody,

4)  he was a witness to the act, with which the case is concerned or in the same case he acted as a witness or as an expert,

5)  he participated in the case in the capacity of a prosecutor, defence counsel, legal representative to a party or conducted preparatory proceedings,

6)  he participated in issuing a judgment or issued an order that was appealed against,

7)  he participated in issuing a judgment that was subsequently reversed,

8)  (repealed)

9)  he participated in issuing a judgment against which an objection was filed,

10)  he conducted mediation.

items.comment:
An interpreter/translator may either be a sworn one (who acquired this position in accordance with the Act of November 25th 2004 on the profession of sworn interpreter) or an ad hoc one, appointed by the investigating authority or the court for the purpose of particular criminal proceedings due to one’s expert knowledge of the language. The act on the profession of sworn interpreter includes several provisions aimed at guaranteeing high quality of their services, including personal qualifications, university degree and the obligation to pass an exam. In case of ad hoc interpreters, assessing whether this knowledge is enough to provide sufficient quality belongs to the investigating authority or the court. Bearing in mind that the authority may not speak the language of the suspect/accused, such mechanism has to be perceived as insufficient. The transposition is thus full with regard to sworn interpreters (translators) but has not been done with regard to ad hoc ones.

It is also worth pointing out that interpretators and translators cannot fulfil their duties if there are reasons to believe that they cannot stay objective due to their relations with the parties or the case itself.

items.text: 2. In order to promote the adequacy of interpretation and translation and efficient access thereto, Member States shall endeavour to establish a register or registers of independent translators and interpreters who are appropriately qualified. Once established, such register or registers shall, where appropriate, be made available to legal counsel and relevant authorities.

nationalActs.title: Ustawa z dnia 25 listopada 2004 r. o zawodzie tłumacza przysięgłego
nationalActs.titleEn: Law of November 25th 2004 on the profession of sworn interpreter (translator)

provisions.textEn:
1. The right to work as a sworn interpreter (translator) is acquired after swearing an oath and being registered on the list of sworn intepreters (translators).

2. A person who swore an oath is ex officio registered on the list run by the Minister of Justice.

1. The entry of a sworn interpreter (translator) on the list contains:

1) surname and name;

2) date and place of birth;

3) citizenship;

4) place of residence;

5) postal address;

6) date of acuqiring professional right to be a sworn interpreter (translator);

7) number of the certificate of sworn interpreter (translator);

8) language or languages covered by the right to be a sworn interpreter (translator);

9) information on disciplinary punishments

10) information on scientific or art titles.

2. A sworn interpreter (translator) is obliged to report any changes of the data contained in the registry within 30 days of such change. The documents proving the change shall be presented.

provisions.comment: The details of the register are regulated in the Regulation of the Minister of Justice of 24 January 2005 on a model certificate attesting to the right to practise the profession of sworn translator and the way in which a list of sworn translators is kept (Dz.U.2005, nr 15, poz. 130).
provisions.textEn: The Minister of Justice makes the register available in the Public Information Biuletin run in accordance with the laws regulating access to public information, excluding the data mentioned in art. 8 sections 1 points 2, 4 and 9.

items.text: 3. Member States shall ensure that interpreters and translators be required to observe confidentiality regarding interpretation and translation provided under this Directive.

provisions.textEn:
1. Sworn interpreter (translator) is obliged to:

1) execute their duties with particular care and impartiality, in accordance with the law,

2) keep in secret facts and circumstances he got to know while interpreting (translating);

3) improve their professional qualifications.

items.comment: The law expressly obliges only sworn interpreters (translators) to observe confidentiality and remains silent as to ad hoc interpreters (translators). One must however bear in mind that most of the interpreters (translators) serving in criminal proceedings are sworn ones.

items.text: Without prejudice to judicial independence and differences in the organisation of the judiciary across the Union, Member States shall request those responsible for the training of judges, prosecutors and judicial staff involved in criminal proceedings to pay special attention to the particularities of communicating with the assistance of an interpreter so as to ensure efficient and effective communication.
items.heading: Article 6

transp.label: No national implementation (either officially nor de facto/indirect)

items.comment: The issue is not specifically mentioned in the programme of training in National School for Judges and Prosecutors.

items.text: Member States shall ensure that when a suspected or accused person has been subject to questioning or hearings by an investigative or judicial authority with the assistance of an interpreter pursuant to Article 2, when an oral translation or oral summary of essential documents has been provided in the presence of such an authority pursuant to Article 3(7), or when a person has waived the right to translation pursuant to Article 3(8), it will be noted that these events have occurred, using the recording procedure in accordance with the law of the Member State concerned.
items.heading: Article 7

nationalActs.titleEn: Law of 6 June 1997 - Code of Criminal Procedure

provisions.textEn:
§ 1. A transcript should contain:

1) an indication of the procedure, its time, place and a list of participating persons,

2) the course of the procedure as well as statements and conclusions of participants thereto,

3) any decisions and orders issued in the course of the procedure, and if a decision or an order was issued separately, the mention of its issue,

4) a description of other circumstances which concern the course of the procedure, if necessary.

§ 2. Explanations, testimonies, declarations, requests and statements concerning specific circumstances made by the agency conducting a procedure are recorded in the transcript with the greatest possible accuracy. Persons participating in the procedure may demand that everything that concerns their rights or interests be included in the transcript with the greatest possible accuracy.
